solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Amusing time on railway marking those passing?

parts.note: something amusing is fun
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A jokey question about whether a comic interlude on the railway might commemorate people travelling past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those passing' sounds like passers-by on a train; here it means the dead, who have passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Funeral monuments and rites commemorate people who have died, the sense of 'passing' as dying.

clue.text: Have nothing to do in strike? A WC needs sorting out

parts.note: to beat is to strike
a loo is a WC, a lavatory

indicators.note: sorting out the letters of 'needs' puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone idle during a strike notices the toilet needs attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action; it is a verb. 'sorting out' is the anagram signal for the final word of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being idle with no occupation, exactly having nothing to do.

clue.text: Not many will follow dog when one's told to stay in

definitions.text: when one's told to stay in

indicators.note: the phrase puts the second piece after the first in the answer

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
few means not many

explanation.surface: A dog-training scene: few dogs will obey when told to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay in' looks like a command to a dog; it is a time people must remain indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is a fixed time after which people are required to remain at home.

clue.text: Everything's thrown into awful song

indicators.note: thrown into puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: awful means bad
everything is all; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a terrible song has everything thrown into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative or sentimental song.

clue.text: Spot old Liberal interrupting record speech

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking in between the other pieces

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
an oration is a formal speech
L abbreviates Liberal, the British political party

explanation.surface: Pick out an aged Liberal heckling a speech that is being recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a verb meaning notice; it is a noun, a stain. This is the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain or mark that changes the colour of a surface is a spot.

clue.text: Small and crudely built house is closed

parts.note: a hut is a rough, simple dwelling

explanation.surface: A tiny ramshackle dwelling is shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut and closed are synonyms, both describing something not open.

clue.text: Boyfriend outside university runs office

indicators.note: outside says the first piece wraps around the others

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A boyfriend, having left university, runs an office.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is an office or agency, such as a travel bureau.

clue.text: A sunny land

parts.note: a sunny room is light, full of daylight

explanation.surface: A description of a sunlit country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun, a country; it is the verb, to come down.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to descend and settle, as a bird lands on a branch.

clue.text: London borough losing billions in income from tenants

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped

parts.note: Brent is a borough in north-west London

explanation.surface: A London council loses billions in housing revenue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is the payment a landlord receives from people occupying the property.

clue.text: Girl's troubled life before London, perhaps

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next
troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: London is an example of a city

explanation.surface: A young woman's unhappy life before moving to the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Consecrated building that's large and outstanding

parts.note: a hall is a large building or room
a debt still outstanding is owed

explanation.surface: A church described as sacred, big and impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed ground is sacred ground, made holy by blessing.

clue.text: For instance, Oscar is a big personality

parts.note: e.g. means for instance
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde, perhaps, offered as an example of a larger-than-life character.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen sense of self-importance is a big personality in the vain sense.

clue.text: Good fortune daring to sacrifice pawn

indicators.note: to sacrifice something is to give it up, so a letter is removed

parts.note: pluck is courage or daring
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess player's luck in a bold pawn sacrifice.
explanation.definitionFit: Luck is chance success, a synonym for good fortune.

clue.text: Computer-aided design incorporates art, see, in large amount

indicators.note: incorporates means takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Design software takes in a large amount of artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartload, literally what fills a cart, is used informally for a great quantity.

clue.text: Error starting the yearbook's print output

indicators.note: starting points to the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A mistake appears at the start of a printed yearbook.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing or printing mistake, a kind of error.

clue.text: Large hat with dark brow lacking covering

parts.note: sombre means dark or gloomy

indicators.note: lacking its covering means the outer letters of the word are stripped off

explanation.surface: A big hat worn with a frown, leaving the brow uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a wide-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Years attached to shop floor

indicators.note: attached to puts the first piece on the end of the other

parts.note: a store is a shop

explanation.surface: An old shop floor, joined on years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level of a building, like a floor.

clue.text: Blend mix of gin and lemon? That's not on

indicators.note: a mix of the words means their letters are shuffled

parts.note: these letters are taken away from the mixed pool, as 'not on' says

explanation.surface: A cocktail-maker asks whether gin and lemon blend, and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not on' sounds like disapproval; it tells you to remove two letters from the pool before 'mix of' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To mingle is to mix or combine things together.

clue.text: Better public school around West African city

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

indicators.note: around says the school wraps the other piece

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A public-school travel plan ranking a West African city above others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like part of 'West African'; it gives only W. Cape Town is in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Town is a major city in South Africa.

clue.text: Article with no name? Then it's this

definitions.text: Article with no name? Then it's this

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece with no byline is credited this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for anonymous, the word credits a piece whose writer is unknown.

clue.text: Some metal creates fine powder

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A metalworking process that grinds metal into dust.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into a fine powder for the skin.

clue.text: Stand lazily round during fencing thrust

indicators.note: during says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a lunge is a thrust in fencing
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A fencer idles about in the middle of an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to loll or stand about in a relaxed, idle way.

clue.text: An idiot backed hard bathroom sponge

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front

parts.note: a fool is an idiot
H abbreviates hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fool supported a tough sponge in the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses A FOOL to make LOOFA.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is the fibrous dried fruit of a gourd used as a bath sponge.
